transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-21
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~65 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Park (Redwood AE), Daniel Kim (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (Levana Procurement), Carlos Rivera (Levana Security), Lena Cho (Levana Legal), Ibrahim Khan (Levana IT Ops)

00:00 Sophie: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm sophie from redwood, account executive. we have daniel here from solutions engineering. how's everybody doing?
00:07 Maya: hi sophie, doing well, thanks. we have a quick agenda, mostly procurement questions, msas, dpa, slas, pricing approvals and onboarding steps.
00:15 Daniel: great, i'll tag in on the technical bits, but first wanted to confirm the setup - you're looking at a dedicated or private deployment, right?
00:22 Maya: yes, we need either dedicated or private; due to PHI concerns and state residency rules some of our data needs to stay in our VPC. also we want customer-managed KMS.
00:31 Sophie: understood. on the legal side we sent the standard redwood msa and dpa, i think lena had a few redlines?
00:36 Lena: yes - we flagged section 5 on data processing, also want stronger audit rights and an explicit data residency clause.
00:43 Sophie: ok that's helpful, we'll review. quick note that our privacy team typically supports both customer-managed KMS and brings in SOC 2 artifacts - daniel can share the runbook for private deployments.
00:51 Carlos: can you confirm if redwood will support HSM integrations? our security policy requires HSM for key management for some regulated workloads.
00:56 Daniel: yes, we have KMS/HSM integrations; for private deployments we can plug into your KMS or HSM via standard connectors. caveats: latency and key wrap ops can add a small overhead, but it's supported.
01:04 Ibrahim: and about network, do you require egress rules or do you support full VPC peering?
01:09 Daniel: we do VPC peering and private link options; we can provide the exact CIDR and port list in the onboarding doc.
01:15 Maya: on slas - our procurement needs a 99.9% uptime SLA for the dedicated pool and response times for severity 1 incidents. can redwood commit to that?
01:24 Sophie: for Dedicated we offer SLA-backed uptime, yes; specifics can be in the contract. for hosted tiers the SLA differs. we'll propose 99.9% for your committed nodes, with a defined credit table.
01:33 Lena: also want RTO and RPO for backups and KV cache persistence spelled out.
01:38 Daniel: RTO/RPO vary by deployment; for Dedicated we can commit to backup frequency and restore windows - we'll include targets in the SLA exhibit.
01:44 Maya: pricing - procurement needs the final price sheet for Dedicated capacity, plus any one-time onboarding fees and estimated monthly costs based on our volume estimate.
01:52 Sophie: yes, i'll include the pricing worksheet with committed capacity tiers and burst pricing. quick question, who's owning internal approvals and timeline?
01:59 Maya: i'll own procurement approvals, target to have approvals by end of year, but legal review might push into january.
02:05 Sophie: understood, we'll aim to get docs to you this week.
02:10 [02:10] Daniel: slight transcript note - sorry - we sometimes call our private product "Redwood Private" in docs, but external templates might say "Private Deployment".
02:18 Carlos: security artifacts - we need SOC 2 type 2 report, pen test summary, and encryption architecture. also, can you confirm data retention and deletion procedures?
02:27 Daniel: SOC 2 and pentest summary are standard; retention is configurable, and we support deletion APIs plus certificate of deletion for private deployments. we'll share the security bundle.
02:35 Lena: on indemnities and liability caps - we typically ask for carveouts for willful misconduct, and negotiation on breach definitions.
02:42 Sophie: thanks, lena - we can take those redlines and route to legal for review and provide a response in the redlined msa/dpa. some items may be standard no-ops, others will need legal sign-off.
02:51 Maya: about procurement gating - we need a price approval from our finance committee; what's the timeline for getting a final quote?
02:56 Sophie: i'll push an updated quote and committed capacity options by 2026-12-23, that should give you time for the finance review.
03:03 Ibrahim: operationally, for the pilot, will we get access to a staging cluster and can we run our evals? we want to run latency, throughput and sample prompt tests.
03:11 Daniel: yes, pilot usually includes a staging environment with a pinned model and telemetry; we'll provide a benchmark harness and sample prompts - we can also run a joint benchmark if you want.
03:19 Maya: great. do you provide data residency reports for states? we have some customers in california and new york with specific rules.
03:25 Daniel: we can configure region pinning and provide region residency attestations for the nodes.
03:31 Carlos: one more - logging and audit trails, how long are logs kept and can we ship logs to our SIEM?
03:36 Daniel: logs can be shipped to your SIEM via forwarder or syslog, retention depends on plan; we can keep audit logs for the length you require as an add-on.
03:44 Lena: can we add a clause about annual security reviews and cooperative audits?
03:49 Sophie: yes, we commonly include cooperative audit language; we'll propose acceptable timeframes in the DPA exhibit.
03:55 Maya: okay, next steps - send docs, pricing, and schedule the pilot kickoff.
04:01 Sophie: recap - sophie to send redlined MSA + DPA + pricing worksheet (by 12/23), daniel to share onboarding runbook and dedicated checklist (by 12/24), carlos to give SOC2 and controls list (by 12/28). we'll target a pilot start 2027-01-10 for two weeks. sound right?
04:14 Maya: yes that works.
04:17 Ibrahim: one small thing, latency SLOs - can you share typical p95/p99 numbers for the model families when running on dedicated gpus?
04:24 Daniel: yes - for our optimized open models on A100-equivalent infra, p95 token latency for short prompts is ~80-150ms depending on prompt size and kv cache hit rate; p99 can be higher. we'll add a small performance exhibit with numbers and test methodology.
04:40 Sophie: i'll include that in the benchmark spreadsheet. any other questions?
04:44 Lena: none from legal for now.
04:46 Maya: nothing else. thanks everyone.
04:49 Sophie: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with the artifacts.
04:52 [04:52] Call ended.
